svg.title: Judge · Jury · Voter: Nash bargaining over what to fix
svg.desc: Every bundle of fixes a panel could choose, placed by its revision cost and weighted Nash objective. The broker searches within the budget to the settlement. Below, five Judges move from independent scores to deliberated ones and the Voter finds the consensus.

g.text: revision cost of the bundle, c(S)

svg.text: 256 bundles a five-Judge panel could choose, drawn from the kernel.
Solid: fits the budget and keeps every veto. Hollow: no deal.
A swarm of review agents, settled by bargaining, not a vote.

g.text: uᵢ(S) = Σf∈S vᵢ(f) − aᵢ · c(S) / n
a Judge's utility: the findings it values, less its share of the rework
D = the credible vetoes · feasible S ⊇ D, c(S) ≤ B
a blocker counts only with a veto behind it; the rest is cheap talk
Nash (1950): the weighted product of each party's gain over no deal
= maxS Σi wᵢ φ(gᵢ), φ(g) = ln(1+g) if g > 0, else g
the kernel's form: concave on gains, so surplus is spread, not piled
blocking in its own area never pays, so ratifying S* is a Nash equilibrium
SURPLUS OVER NO DEAL, BY JUDGE

svg.text: A LIVE PANEL, SCORES OUT OF 5 · INDEPENDENT → AFTER THE JURY → CONSENSUS
